_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); revenue, net-to-gross, expense, receivables and operating-margin signals with Visa's rule-T thresholds

pit_profile.why: 'Visa Inc. (“Visa” or the “Company”) is a global payments technology company that connects consumers, businesses, banks and governments in more than 200 countries and territories, enabling them to use digital currency instead of cash and checks.' 'Our business is affected by overall economic conditions and consumer spending.' 'Within the general purpose payment card industry, we face substantial and intense competition worldwide in the provision of payments services to financial institution clients and their cardholder merchants.' 'Of note this fiscal year, the Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act was signed into law in the United States on July 21, 2010, which will, amongst other things, regulate interchange fees and transaction routing rules related to our debit card products.'; no 10-K calls the business cyclical (the economy and spending are a 'why', not the company's own label: the LOW, SHW and JPM reading), so the kind is DURABLE; no disruption theme in taxonomy_eras.json is live for a payments network on these dates, so the watch list is empty

BEAR.desc: EPS +0.0%/yr (worst year FY09-FY10, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +20.9%/yr (FY11 revenue guide + margin + buyback); P/E at its 2.5-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +26.1%/yr (FY09-FY10 CAGR, at least BASE); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +26.1%/yr (no 2-yr run in FY09-FY10: BULL's rate); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: V (retrospective, 2011-04-08) ◉ BUY — Ratio B 0.17x (12.9% downside to Bear $66.86 / +73.5% upside to Bull $133.11) | Adj composite 2.38 vs market 1.79: gap +0.59 [UNDERVALUED] | +31% above the EPP floor $58.65 (15x FY11E $3.91) | Conservative 2-yr case: +38.4% total (+19.2%/yr) | At 19.6x FY11E the 15% hurdle price $101.46 sits at or below the BASE case; revenue +14.2% YoY in Q1 FY11, forward revenues +11-15% (FY11 net revenue growth guide); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
